name: HR-Bench
ability_definition: The ability to see details at a distance.

task_realism.reasoning: Picking out colour, material and embedded text on small objects in large real-world photos is close to what far-vision work involves, such as reading distant signage or identifying a far-off vehicle or person. However, the objects are small because of image resolution, not necessarily physical distance. Part of the FCP set also uses charts and maps, which have no link to seeing at a distance.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Conditions differ a lot from real work. Inputs are static, pre-captured 8K frames with no motion, no changing light or weather, and no atmospheric haze varied as a controlled factor. There is also no time pressure, no chance to reposition or refocus, and no safety stakes. Real far-vision tasks such as driving, lifeguarding, surveillance or aviation involve live, dynamic scenes and quick detection.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers fine attribute recognition and some cross-object relations for small targets, which is a real piece of far vision. It leaves out several other parts of the ability: judging distance and depth, detecting and tracking moving targets at range, and noticing a distant hazard without being asked about it. It does not control or label viewing distance, and the non-distance chart and map items dilute the construct.

format_match.reasoning: Hand-written multiple-choice questions about a single photo are an artificial format. Real work needs open-ended detection, identification and reporting, such as 'there is a person in the water 200 m out' or 'the sign reads X', usually without a prompt pointing to what to look for.

transferability_reasoning: HR-Bench does test resolving fine details of visually small objects in realistic high-resolution photos, which is a meaningful proxy for part of far vision. It is limited by static, prompted, multiple-choice evaluation, no control of physical distance, and off-construct chart and map items. The result is modest transfer to real workplace far-vision capability.

2025.metric: accuracy (%), HR-Bench 8K overall (average of FSP and FCP)
2025.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal or corrected vision, inspecting the same 8K images on a display with ordinary pan/zoom and no time pressure.

2026.model_or_system: SCCM-based RFT model (built on a Pixel-Reasoner baseline)
2026.metric: accuracy (%), HR-Bench 8K overall (average of FSP and FCP)
2026.human_reference: General working adults with normal or corrected vision who inspect fine details in large high-resolution imagery (e.g., inspectors, analysts, general visual work)
